title: The Tale of Peter Rabbit
description: Peter visits a dangerous garden, loses his clothes, and returns home tired.
text: Peter Rabbit went into Mr. McGregor's garden even though his mother told him not to go. He ate lettuce, beans, and radishes. Mr. McGregor saw him and chased him with a rake. Peter lost his shoes and his blue jacket. At home, his mother gave him chamomile tea.

title: A Scandal in Bohemia
description: The King of Bohemia asks Holmes to recover an embarrassing photograph from Irene Adler.

title: The Architecture of Human Cognition and AI
description: A comparison of biological cognition, artificial neural networks, and neuro-symbolic systems.
text: Modern AI extracts patterns from enormous datasets, while biological intelligence uses different computational principles. The prefrontal cortex coordinates executive functions, including task switching and working memory. Brain plasticity supports learning from scarce input. Artificial networks can suffer catastrophic forgetting. Neuromorphic systems imitate biological synapses, while a hybrid neuro-symbolic framework could combine neural learning with algorithmic reasoning.

title: A Picnic in the Park
description: Anna and Leo prepare a simple picnic and make a new friend in the park.
text: Anna and Leo went to the park on Saturday morning. They brought sandwiches, apples, and a bottle of water. After lunch, they played badminton near a tall tree. A small dog ran after the shuttlecock, so its owner came to apologize. The children invited the owner to sit with them, and everyone shared the last apple.

title: The Community Garden
description: Neighbours transform an unused city lot into a garden that teaches cooperation and patience.
text: An empty lot between two apartment buildings had collected rubbish for years. A group of residents proposed turning it into a community garden. They removed the waste, built wooden beds, and planted vegetables. The first harvest was small because the soil needed care. By autumn, however, neighbours were sharing tomatoes and teaching children how food grows.

title: Why Cities Need Quiet Places
description: An exploration of how quiet public spaces can support attention, health, and civic life.
text: Urban life offers opportunity, but constant noise can place a hidden burden on attention. Quiet public spaces, from small courtyards to protected parks, give residents a chance to recover from stimulation. Their value is not merely aesthetic. Such places can support reflection, conversation, and inclusive access to the city. Planning them requires balancing transport, commerce, and the need for restorative environments.
